findings.title: Speech detached from disclosed warrant
findings.claim: The denied knowledge and the ongoing act of saying meet wider examples of inherited conjecture and mouth-level profession, making the great word an utterance whose social repetition cannot supply the knowledge it lacks.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries knowledge in عِلْمٍ and audible saying in يَقُولُونَ. 6:148 tests inherited claims by asking for knowledge that can be brought forth, while 5:41 places mouth-level profession beside lies and distortion; those wider relations return through the two focus words and change the force of greatness from mere size to socially effective but evidentially empty assertion.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why repetition and public force do not turn a claim into knowledge: the ayah is exposing an output channel that has become detached from disclosed reality.
findings.containment: The direct meaning remains that the speakers and their forefathers have no knowledge and say only lies. This finding does not declare every repeated statement false, and it does not replace the ayah's specific accusation with a general theory of speech.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run record directly anchors both focus branches; the selected connection rows provide independent wider triggers, while legacy duplicate nominations are represented rather than used to raise the claim beyond its typed support.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi bilme, tanıma ve gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavrama durumu bilgisizliğin karşıtıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The indefinite noun عِلْمٍ names knowing and grasping what is true, and the surrounding negation removes that knowledge from the claim.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 6:148 asks whether the inherited religious claim can produce knowledge and contrasts such knowledge with conjecture and fabrication.
branch_activations.activation: The wider evidentiary test returns through the focus's denied knowledge: inheritance and repetition can preserve a claim socially without making it disclosed understanding.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The great word is publicly weighty but epistemically empty because its circulation has not supplied the knowledge it lacks.
branch_activations.boundary: The contact sharpens the ayah's denial of warrant; it does not say that every inherited or repeated claim is false.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: The imperfect يَقُولُونَ depicts an ongoing act of putting speech into sound, which the final restriction identifies as falsehood.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:41 places mouth-level profession beside listening to lies and the distortion of words.
branch_activations.activation: The wider speech relation returns through the focus's ongoing saying and its mouth-centered setting, making public profession part of the evidentiary problem rather than a neutral report.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The utterance is an outward channel that can carry social force while remaining detached from inward assent and truth.
branch_activations.boundary: This concerns the gap between spoken profession and truth in the focus claim; it is not a universal condemnation of speech.

findings.title: The utterance as a qualified wound image
findings.claim: The focus word كَلِمَةً can be heard as a discrete, materially consequential utterance: its grave magnitude and exit from mouths let the supplied wider scene of 18:6 register false speech as something that can mark and injure its hearer, while the ordinary accusation remains intact.
findings.mechanism: كَلِمَةً is the carrier. كَبُرَتْ supplies grave magnitude, تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ supplies bodily exit, and the legacy wide walk names 18:6 as the contextual return. The B002 word-unit and B003 wound facets meet at an utterance leaving a body and having an effect on another body.
findings.reader_payoff: A translation's great word becomes more than abstract magnitude: the claim appears as a public object capable of wounding without making that image the literal syntax.
findings.containment: The direct referent remains a spoken false claim. The trusted cross-run row is itself marked as a rejected review result, and the wide walk explicitly gives proximity rather than causation; the bodily injury is therefore a contained, qualified analogy rather than a claim that the text describes a literal wound.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and nominated facets are exact, but the wider 18:6 return is supplied by a legacy-unbound reader walk and is explicitly limited to proximity; the source conflict and causal uncertainty remain visible.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek, tek başına anlam taşıyan bir harf veya harflerden oluşmuş tek bir söz birimidir.
branch_activations.carrier: كَلِمَةً names one bounded speech unit rather than an undifferentiated atmosphere of talk.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: كَبُرَتْ assigns the unit grave magnitude and تَخْرُجُ places that unit in bodily emergence from mouths.
branch_activations.activation: The discrete word is made publicly encounterable by its grave scale and oral exit, so the false assertion is heard as an object with social presence rather than only as an abstract proposition.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The claim becomes a socially present utterance whose public force can exceed the evidence behind it.
branch_activations.boundary: B002 supplies the bounded word-unit; it does not itself mean bodily injury, which belongs to the separately qualified B003 contact.
